QuestionStmt.S: Which carbon atom of glucopyranose numbered from C–1 to C–6 is anomeric?

Solution.S:
In glucopyranose (the cyclic form of glucose), the anomeric carbon is the one that was part of the carbonyl group (aldehyde) in the open-chain form. Upon cyclization, this carbon becomes the hemiacetal carbon and is designated as C–1. The hydroxyl group at C–1 can be in either α or β position, giving rise to anomers.

Thus, the anomeric carbon is C–1, which corresponds to option D.
